title: A pretty-tight converse on the classical capacity of generalized amplitude-damping channels
abstract: The classical capacity of a quantum channel is the highest rate at which classical information can be transmitted with vanishing error. Although the capacities of many fundamental quantum channels have been established, the capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping channel remains an open problem in quantum Shannon theory. In this work, we revisit a converse bound introduced by Brandão et al. [Phys. Rev. Lett. 106, 230502 (2011)], which upper-bounds the classical capacity in terms of a correlation measure. For the generalized amplitude-damping channel, we derive a relaxation of this measure that makes the converse bound efficiently computable. Numerical comparisons demonstrate that our bound is pretty tight in general and nearly coincides with the Holevo information at nonzero temperatures, significantly improving upon existing bounds across the entire parameter range.
summary: This paper tackles the open problem of finding the classical capacity for the generalized amplitude-damping channel. The authors derive a new, computable upper bound, $U_G(\gamma, N)$, by refining existing correlation measures. This bound is shown to be highly accurate, providing significant theoretical progress in quantum Shannon theory for open quantum systems.
main_problem: The primary goal is to determine a tight converse bound on the classical capacity of the generalized amplitude-damping channel (GADC).
main_result: The authors derive an upper bound, $U_G(\gamma, N)$, for the classical capacity, which is shown to be pretty tight and nearly coincides with the Holevo information at non-zero temperatures.
method: The work revisits and refines a converse bound by deriving a computable relaxation of an existing correlation measure, utilizing techniques involving entanglement of formation and bounding conditional entropies.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the generalized amplitude-damping channel (GADC), which models spin-relaxation ($T_1$) due to coupling to a thermal bath at non-zero temperature. The analysis is performed on qubits.
key_observables: Classical capacity $C(A_{\gamma,N})$, Holevo information $\chi(A_{\gamma,N})$, output entropy $S(B_n)$, and correlation measures $g_E^{\gamma,N}(q)$ and $g_B^{\gamma,N}(q)$.
important_parameters: Damping probability $\gamma$, equilibrium occupation probability $N$, and input occupation probability $q$.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on bounding the Holevo information using the entanglement of formation and applying convexity arguments to simplify correlation measures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the derived bound $U_G$ against the Holevo rate $\chi$ and other known bounds across varying $N$ values. Figure 2 examines the residual gap between $U_G$ and $\chi$ in the entanglement-breaking regime.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the upper bound $C(A_{\gamma,N}) \le U_G(\gamma, N)$ by bounding the Holevo information using correlation measures derived from the environment and output measurements. Subsequent sections refine these bounds by proving the optimality of the measurement strategies used in the penalty terms.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical tool (a tight converse bound) for characterizing the fundamental information limits of a physically relevant open quantum system model (GADC).
